package target

import "github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go"

// classify pins its model with a symbolic constant.
// The literal "claude-opus-4-8" also appears in this comment, and in the string below,
// to prove the codemod anchors on the AST and not on text.
func classify(client *anthropic.Client) {
	_ = "claude-opus-4-8 is mentioned here but must never be rewritten"
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{Model: anthropic.ModelClaudeOpus4_6})
}

// agent never sets a model at all — the override must INSERT the field.
func agent(client *anthropic.Client) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{})
}

// ── prompt call sites ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// These are the shape the registry's `prompt: {field: "params.Messages"}` locator actually points at
// in the real SDK: a message CONSTRUCTION, never a bare string argument. The prompt text is a string
// literal nested inside it. Note the role is carried by the FUNCTION (NewUserMessage), not by a
// string — which is why the text literal is the construction's only one, and why it can be located
// without any per-SDK knowledge in the rewriter.

// summarize's prompt is a fixed string inside the construction.
func summarize(client *anthropic.Client) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{
		Model:    anthropic.ModelClaudeSonnet4,
		Messages: []anthropic.MessageParam{anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("Summarize the ticket."))},
	})
}

// triage builds its prompt from a literal and a runtime variable. This is what a template with a
// {{ticket}} slot has to bind to: the slot's value is the Go expression `ticket`, not a string the
// codemod could ever know.
func triage(client *anthropic.Client, ticket string) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{
		Messages: []anthropic.MessageParam{anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("Triage this ticket: " + ticket))},
	})
}

// chat is a two-turn conversation: two text literals, so a single prompt template cannot say which
// turn it replaces. The engine must refuse rather than pick one.
func chat(client *anthropic.Client) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{
		Messages: []anthropic.MessageParam{
			anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("First question.")),
			anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("Second question.")),
		},
	})
}

// wrapped spreads one prompt expression across two lines. Replacing it with a one-line expression
// would delete a line and shift every line below it — the minimality gate's job to catch.
func wrapped(client *anthropic.Client, ticket string) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{
		Messages: []anthropic.MessageParam{anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("Ticket: " +
			ticket))},
	})
}

// ── tool / skill call sites ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// P14: binding a skill CONSTRUCTS the SDK tool value rather than replacing an expression, so these
// two call sites are the whole of what the materializer has to tell apart.

// toolbound writes its tool list out at the call site. A skill binding REPLACES that written list —
// the engine can see exactly what it is dropping, so replacing it is not a guess.
func toolbound(client *anthropic.Client) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{Tools: []anthropic.ToolUnionParam{}})
}

// dynamictools assembles its tool set at runtime. Overwriting it would silently discard whatever
// buildTools() returned — the same silent data loss an interpolated prompt is refused for — so the
// engine must refuse rather than guess what the runtime set holds.
func dynamictools(client *anthropic.Client, buildTools func() []anthropic.ToolUnionParam) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{Tools: buildTools()})
}

// prunable writes three tools on one line — the shape a prune deletes an element out of.
func prunable(client *anthropic.Client) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{Tools: []anthropic.ToolUnionParam{weatherTool, sqlTool, searchTool}})
}

// stackedtools writes one tool per line. A deletion here must not close the line up: removing a line
// would shift every line below it and invalidate the build gate's file:line attribution.
func stackedtools(client *anthropic.Client) {
	client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{Tools: []anthropic.ToolUnionParam{
		weatherTool,
		sqlTool,
	}})
}
